annotationRationale: Integrality strengthens the strict inequalities into gaps of at least one, proving a denominator bound. A unique integer numerator at that bound supplies an attaining fraction.
sourceMethod: Followed the official positive-integer-gap argument by adding the two fractional distances, then checked the numerator interval at denominator 16.

review.mathCheck: Strict inequalities and integrality give 9p−5q≥1 and 4q−7p≥1. Their weighted sum yields 1/63≥16/(63q), hence q≥16. At q=16, 80/9<p<64/7 has exactly the integer p=9. Thus q−p=7, choice A; neither endpoint is admitted.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of the main official solution 17 on page 10. It preserves the integer-gap denominator bound and verifies attainment and numerator uniqueness without requiring the Farey-fraction theorem.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed nodes capture the bound-and-attainment argument and integer numerator selection. Inequality properties appropriately serve as background.
